subject: computer-science
title: Computer Systems: Von Neumann Architecture
welcome_lead: Inside the classic CPU model that powers nearly every computer.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: von Neumann architecture, the FDE cycle and core registers.
final_note: Once you know the cycle, every CPU behaviour makes sense.

concepts.def: The stored-program design in which instructions and data share one main memory and are moved over shared buses to the processor.
The register holding the memory address of the next instruction; it is incremented during fetch, or overwritten by jumps and branches.
The register that holds the address of the memory location about to be read from or written to.
The register that temporarily holds data or an instruction transferred between the processor and main memory.
A general-purpose register in which the results of calculations performed by the arithmetic logic unit are held.
The address bus carries memory addresses, the data bus carries the data itself, and the control bus carries control and timing signals.

walkthroughs.body_html: John von Neumann's design uses a single memory for both instructions and data, a CPU with control and ALU, and a bus to move data. Harvard architecture is the alternative, with separate memories.
Every instruction: fetch from memory at PC, decode in the control unit, execute in the ALU. The PC is then incremented (or set by a branch) and the cycle repeats.
The PC tracks the next instruction. The MAR and MDR sit between the CPU and memory. The IR holds the current instruction. The ACC stores arithmetic results.

mcqs.q: After an instruction is fetched, what normally happens to the program counter?
options: It is incremented to hold the address of the next instruction
It is wiped to zero
It stores the result of the calculation
It is moved to the hard disk
Data or instructions just read from, or about to be written to, memory
The address of the next instruction
The CPU temperature
The list of running programs

mcqs.q: The von Neumann bottleneck refers to:
options: The shared bus between processor and memory limiting the rate of data transfer
The small size of modern keyboards
Slow internet connections
The limited number of USB ports

mcqs.q: Read and write signals are carried by which bus?
options: The control bus
The address bus
The data bus
The expansion bus

mcqs.q: Does the program counter hold the instruction currently being executed?
options: No - the PC holds the ADDRESS of the next instruction to fetch; the fetched instruction itself is held in the current instruction register.
Yes - the program counter counts completed instructions.
Yes - buses are software, not physical connections.
Yes - the program counter contains the instruction being run.

mcqs.q: Does the accumulator store memory addresses?
options: No - the accumulator holds data, specifically the results of ALU operations; addresses are held in the PC and MAR.
Yes - the accumulator accumulates the addresses of used memory.
Yes - the accumulator is part of the hard drive.
Yes - buses are software, not physical connections.

mcqs.q: Are the address bus and the data bus the same set of wires?
options: No - they are separate buses: the address bus says WHERE in memory to look, while the data bus carries WHAT is being transferred.
Yes - one shared bus carries both addresses and data simultaneously.
Yes - the program counter counts completed instructions.
Yes - buses are software, not physical connections.
